title_jp: {友達|ともだち}と{予定|よてい}
context: You've made friends with other volunteers and a local your age. Time to make weekend plans, in casual Japanese.

phrases.jp: {週末|しゅうまつ}、{空|あ}いてる？
{一緒|いっしょ}に{行|い}かない？
phrases.note: A negative question is an invitation. Very common.

phrases.jp: {何時|なんじ}にどこで{待|ま}ち{合|あ}わせる？
phrases.en: What time and where shall we meet?

phrases.jp: すみません、その{日|ひ}はちょっと…
phrases.en: Sorry, that day is a bit…
phrases.note: Trailing off with ちょっと… is how you say no politely. With friends: ごめん、その{日|ひ}はちょっと…

dialogue_setting: Texting and chatting with a local friend.

dialogue.speaker: Friend
dialogue.jp: ねえ、{土曜日|どようび}{空|あ}いてる？
dialogue.en: Hey, are you free on Saturday?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: うん、{空|あ}いてるよ。どうしたの？

dialogue.speaker: Friend
dialogue.jp: お{祭|まつ}りがあるんだけど、{一緒|いっしょ}に{行|い}かない？
dialogue.en: There's a festival. Want to go together?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: いいね、{行|い}こう！{何時|なんじ}にする？
dialogue.en: Sounds good, let's go! What time?

dialogue.speaker: Friend
dialogue.jp: 5{時|じ}に{駅前|えきまえ}で{待|ま}ち{合|あ}わせしよう。
dialogue.en: Let's meet in front of the station at 5.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: オッケー、じゃあまたね！

kanji.where: On posters, lanterns and shrine banners. Check the local notice board for {秋祭|あきまつ}り and its date.
kanji.related: Related: {花火大会|はなびたいかい} fireworks show.

tip.title: When to drop です/ます
tip.body: With people your age, once they talk casually to you, it's natural to switch too. With older people and anyone you work for, stay polite until they say otherwise. Mixing is normal: ありがとう！ to a friend, ありがとうございます to their parents.

challenge.prompt: Invite a friend, casually: "Want to go to the onsen together on Sunday?"
challenge.hint: onsen = {温泉|おんせん}, invitation = ～ない？
challenge.model_answer: {日曜日|にちようび}、{一緒|いっしょ}に{温泉|おんせん}{行|い}かない？
